meta.name: English
meta.note: Part codex. Keep the item keys; translate the values. 'lines' is the description, 'tip' is a one-line hint.

hub.title: The Hub King
lines: Six ports, labelled A through F.
A 5x5 light matrix shows pictures and letters.
Centre button = power on / run program.
A gyro that senses tilt, a speaker,
and a rechargeable battery are all inside.
hub.tip: Any port works, but it must match the port in your program.

motorL.title: The Steel Giant
lines: Use it to push heavy things or turn big wheels.
It has a rotation sensor inside, so it knows
exactly how many degrees it has turned.
That is how "exactly one turn" is possible.
motorL.tip: Large for power, Medium for light and fast.

motorM.title: The Twin Runners
lines: For arms, grippers, steering — light, fast moves.
It has a rotation sensor, same as the Large Motor.
It stars in today's build, the flag-waving arm.
motorM.tip: The two look identical. Tell them apart by port.

color.title: The Rainbow Eye
lines: It tells red, blue, yellow and more apart.
It also measures how much light bounces back.
Line following is its classic use.
color.tip: Too close to the floor or too far and it misreads.

dist.title: The Owl Eye
lines: The two eye-like holes send out sound and time
the echo to know how far the object ahead is.
Those eyes are also LEDs you can switch on and off.
dist.tip: Soft cloth or slanted surfaces absorb sound and confuse it.

force.title: The Fist Sentinel
force.one: A hand that feels how hard.
lines: It knows not only that it was pressed,
but how hard, as a number.
You can tell a light press from a firm one.
force.tip: Often used as a bumper to detect collisions.

cable.title: The Joining Thread
lines: Sensor or motor, the plug is always the same.
Only the length differs. Short ones keep it tidy.
Pull the hard plug, never the wire.
cable.tip: Pulling the wire breaks it. Unplug cables first when taking apart.

beam.title: The Bone Piece
lines: The hole count is the length. 7 holes = a 7-beam.
They come straight, L-shaped, and as frames.
Beams join to each other with pins.
beam.tip: Count the holes to find the beam you need. Colour means nothing.

pinBlack.title: The Black Locking Nail
lines: Rough surface = friction = for locking.
The longer 3-length friction pin is blue.
Use this pin to join the frame firmly.
pinBlack.tip: "It won't come out" is not a fault — that's the job. Use the separator.

pinGray.title: The Pale Turning Nail
lines: Shiny surface = no friction = for turning.
Use it for wheels, joints and swinging arms.
Use it where you needed a lock and the robot wobbles.
pinGray.tip: Judge by colour. Black/blue lock, light grey/beige turn.

connector.title: The Key of Direction
lines: It turns a horizontal structure into a vertical one.
The cross hole takes an axle, the round hole a pin.
It often bridges a motor's output axle and a beam.
connector.tip: Look at the hole shape. Cross = axle, circle = pin.

axle.title: The Turning Core
lines: What you fit on it turns with it. It carries force.
You can memorise the length by colour:
odd = light grey, even = black, and 2-long is red.
axle.tip: Unsure of the length? Hold it against beam holes and count.

bush.title: The Stopper
bush.one: A ring that locks an axle.
lines: The 1-length one is grey, the half-length one yellow.
Fit them at both ends so the axle cannot drift.
bush.tip: If the robot keeps going loose, check for a missing bush.

separator.title: The Teardown Tool
separator.one: The safe way to pry parts.
lines: It levers pins and bricks out for you.
Nails and teeth hurt you and damage the parts.
It halves the time a teardown takes.
separator.tip: Slip the pointed end under the pin head and press up slowly.

flag.title: The Victory Flag
lines: It does nothing, but it makes the motion visible.
You can see at a glance how far the motor turned.
flag.tip: Keep it light so the motor has an easy time.
